source_quote: Bleeding or spotting between menstrual periods. This can be caused by something other than endometriosis. If it happens often, you should see your doctor.
note: Weak because the source itself qualifies it in the same breath — "This can be caused by something other than endometriosis." Treating it as strong support would read more into the sentence than it says.

source_quote: Short menstrual cycles (27 days or fewer)
note: IMPERFECT MAPPING. The source's threshold is 27 days; our buckets break at 21 and 35. under_21_days sits inside "27 days or fewer" so the row is true, but it misses cycles of 21-27 days, which the source would also count. Fixing this properly means changing the feature's buckets, which would invalidate other rows — flagged rather than silently fudged.

source_quote: Infertility , or not being able to get pregnant.
note: Listed among the symptoms, but weak: infertility is non-specific and appears under PCOS too, so it separates the differential very little. Retires a previously dead-weight feature.

source_quote: Painful bowel movements or pain when urinating during menstrual periods. In rare cases, you may also find blood in your stool or urine.
note: Cyclical bowel and bladder pain is distinctive: the timing tie to menstruation is what makes it point at endometriosis rather than at a bowel or urinary condition.

source_quote: Pain during or after sex. This is usually described as a "deep" pain and is different from pain felt at the entrance to the vagina when penetration begins.
note: One of the most discriminating features in the differential — neither PCOS nor fibroids is characterised by it. The source goes out of its way to distinguish deep from entrance pain, which is characteristic framing rather than a bare list entry. This row also retires a feature that was previously dead weight.

source_quote: Pain. This is the most common symptom. Women with endometriosis may have many different kinds of pain.
note: THE ELIMINATION ROW for endometriosis. The source frames pain as THE most common symptom, not merely one entry in a list — characteristic framing, which is what the protocol requires before an argues_against row may be written. Without it, endometriosis never drops out of the differential. Note this is weaker grounds than the PCOS elimination row: "most common" is a statement about frequency, not a diagnostic criterion. If you think that is too thin, drop this row and accept that endometriosis will need a positive finding elsewhere to be eliminated.

source_quote: Very painful menstrual cramps. The pain may get worse over time.
note: Weak rather than strong because "very painful" is not a severity scale and our severe level means "stops you doing normal activities". The row covers part of what the source says; the progression over time has no feature.

source_quote: Chronic (long-term) pain in the lower back and pelvis
note: Endometriosis pain is not confined to periods, which is part of what separates it from ordinary period pain. Weak because "chronic" describes duration rather than the constant-through-the-cycle pattern our value names.

source_quote: Pelvic pain , which often happens during your period
note: Named as THE main symptom: the source introduces it with "The main symptoms of endometriosis are:". Corroborated by the Office on Women's Health, which says "Pain. This is the most common symptom."

source_quote: Menstrual periods that last more than seven days
note: Exact mapping onto our over_7_days bucket, which is rare and worth noting. Weak because the source lists it under "You might be more likely to get endometriosis if you have" — a risk factor, not a presenting sign.

source_quote: Severe acne which may be hard to treat.
note: Listed, but not framed as characteristic, so weak rather than strong. Acne is common enough in the general population that treating it as strong support would raise PCOS on very little.

source_quote: Skipped periods—called oligomenorrhea
note: Skipped periods lengthen the interval between them. Weak because the source names the pattern rather than a day threshold, so the mapping to our over_35_days bucket is ours.

source_quote: Menstrual irregularities: No menstrual periods—called amenorrhea
note: Absent periods are named explicitly, not merely implied by "irregular".

source_quote: Irregular or missed menstrual periods.
note: Listed first among the symptoms of PCOS, and corroborated by NICHD, which calls absence of ovulation a characteristic feature.

source_quote: Because the characteristic features of PCOS (also known as Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovary Syndrome [PMOS])—absence of ovulation, indicated by irregular menstrual periods or no periods at all; high androgen levels; and growths in one or both ovaries, often clumps of ovarian follicles that have stopped developing—are wide ranging, so, too, are the symptoms of the condition.
note: THE ELIMINATION ROW. The source frames absence of ovulation as a CHARACTERISTIC feature and states it is indicated by irregular or absent periods, so regular cycles argue against — this is explicit framing, not inference from a symptom list, which the protocol forbids. MedlinePlus corroborates diagnostically: "People with PCOS usually have at least two of these problems: Not ovulating...". Without this row PCOS never drops out of the differential and elimination does not work.

source_quote: Infertility . PCOS is one of the most common causes of infertility. But many women with PCOS can still get pregnant.
note: Weak despite strong language, because the same sentence qualifies it: "many women with PCOS can still get pregnant". The source states a population-level association, not a per-person sign.

source_quote: Too much hair on the face, chest, stomach, or thighs.
note: Named as a main sign on both sources; NICHD calls it hirsutism and ties it to high androgen levels, one of the three characteristic features.

source_quote: Obesity , weight gain, or trouble losing weight.
note: IMPERFECT MAPPING, deliberately weak. The source names obesity, which is a state rather than a change, alongside weight gain, which is a change. Our feature captures change only. Weak support reflects that the row covers part of what the source says, not all of it.

source_quote: Heavy or painful periods or bleeding between periods
note: Same sentence as the row above, which is legitimate — one source sentence supports two cells. Weak rather than strong because bleeding between periods appears last in a list of alternatives rather than being emphasised.

source_quote: Heavy or painful periods or bleeding between periods
note: First symptom listed, and corroborated by NICHD ("Heavy bleeding or painful periods") and by the NHS heavy periods page, which names fibroids among the causes.
